questions: How many mean shifts change the actual dispatched command and next observed position?
How often does a large final utility difference occur without a nearest-horizon native damage difference?
Do distance changes to the same initially observed parasite agree with later utility improvements?
measurements: Use only admitted native windows and observed state. Sum exact server_step_effects per exported step; never infer damage from attack commands or reverse reward coefficients. Track initially nearest parasite by its within-capture ID; no value assigned if absent later.
coverage: Require all native provider steps F through F+H-1 and an observed state at F+H for each H. Truncation, death, goal or missing visibility are reported explicitly; no extrapolated positions, zero-filled unknown effects or convenient replacement states.
comparisons: Pair each measured alternative with its own admitted control at identical H. Final utility4*alive_goal+0.25*kills-received/100-death, unchanged from preceding selector protocol. Use absolute final delta>=0.5 as a descriptive large-change band; report all pairs too.
interpretation: A late outcome difference with tied early damage does not prove random label noise or irrelevant movement. Physical state and trajectory may already differ. This audit cannot distinguish inadequate representation from continuation stochasticity by itself.
next: Use measured timing and coverage to predeclare the next representation/horizon/stability experiment. Do not refit rejected selector endpoints or claim improved battle quality.
